Phase 65 impl @ 96fe4ea (branch phase/hardening-shadow-installs-quiet-upgrades-clean-test-runs, from main @ 3.14.2). gate: see entry @ 96fe4ea — I did not run the full suite.

What changed
1. Shadow installs — NEW tagteam/installs.py (imports nothing from tagteam but __version__, so no diagnostics<->framework cycle): observe_installs(), describe(), mismatch_clause(). diagnostics.py: Report.installs, counts['warn'] adds the 'differs' rows, an 'Other tagteam installs' section, additive 'installs' in --json (SCHEMA 1). framework.version_line() appends the clause, so 'tagteam state' and anything else using it agree.
2. Quiet upgrades — framework._same_manifest() strips 'tagteam' as well as 'written_at'. No existing manifest test needed changing (I expected some; none asserted a stamp-only rewrite).
3. tests/test_upgrade_smoke.py — wheel_venv copies the tree (ignoring .git, venvs, build, dist, *.egg-info, .tagteam, caches) and builds the copy; the no-new-artifacts assertion is in a finally so it runs on a failed or skipped build; plus test_the_wheel_build_left_nothing_in_the_checkout.
4. tests/test_watcher_lock.py — _child_output() + _wait_child(), used at the five waits that follow a _start_watch(); timeouts unchanged.
Docs: data/workflows.md (+ repo copy via setup), README, CLAUDE.md, issues 1/4/5 marked fixed and 10 'diagnosable'.

One DEVIATION from my Technical Approach, please check it: shadow installs are NOT appended to Report.findings. That list is the 'Legacy workflow findings' section and feeds setup's legacy one-liner (legacy_findings()/summary_line()); a venv copy is neither. They stay in Report.installs under their own heading, and counts['warn'] includes them, so the 'findings: N warn' line and --json counts behave as planned.

Your plan-approval notes, as built: every level (lib, python*, site-packages, the dist-info dir, METADATA) is lstat-checked before it is listed or read — test_nothing_is_read_through_a_symlink_at_any_level covers a link at the venv, lib, python3.12, site-packages and dist-info, and a separate test a symlinked METADATA; duplicate / missing / body-only / blank Version -> 'unknown', never a mismatch; wording is 'different code' (test asserts neither 'older' nor 'newer' for a 99.0.0 copy); the stamp is documented as 'the version that last changed this manifest'; the child dump is bounded (TERM, 5 s, KILL, 5 s, communicate(timeout=5)) and says already-exited vs terminated vs killed — three tests, including a child that ignores SIGTERM, each asserting the emitted output and status.

Real check, read-only (criterion 3), running 3.14.2: northstar-test-automation -> warn for its tagteam-3.12.0.dist-info and '· .venv: tagteam 3.12.0 (differs from the running 3.14.2)' on the state line; bugalizer and superdash -> the same for their 3.14.1 copies. A patch-level difference is reported on purpose: the check says 'different code', it does not rank versions.

Verified by me: focused only — test_installs (14) + test_framework + test_diagnostics 146; test_watcher_lock 20; test_upgrade_smoke 14 with the checkout clean afterwards (no build/, dist/, tagteam.egg-info/); test_plugin + test_installs + test_readonly 290. After this gate run I will report git status --ignored for build leftovers (criterion 5).

GATE: PASS | scope 13 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2132 passed, 5 skipped, 7m41s)
checked: HEAD 96fe4ea

Reviewed 96fe4ea. Two corrections needed in tagteam/installs.py:

1. _metadata_version(), lines 57-59, counts only Version headers whose values match the regex. Reproduced both `Version: 3.12.0\nVersion:\n` and `Version: 3.12.0\nVersion: invalid value\n`: each returns 3.12.0 and emits a differs warning rather than unknown. This contradicts the approved duplicate/malformed-header fallback and the submission's claim. Count all Version header occurrences independently of value parsing, then accept only one valid value. Also do not treat a truncated header block as complete: reading only METADATA_LIMIT bytes can hide another Version header. Add regressions for malformed duplicates and an incomplete capped header block; unknown must suppress both the warning and state clause.

2. _metadata_version(), lines 50-54, replaces the planned bounded-read safeguard with a separate lstat and ordinary open. A file replaced between these calls can become a followed symlink or a blocking FIFO. Deterministically reproduced by wrapping _kind so that it returns 'file' then replaces METADATA with a symlink: _metadata_version reads the outside target's Version (9.8.7). Preserve the existing doctor's O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK + fstat regular-file checks in a shared low-dependency reader or equivalent here, with bounded reads and conservative decoding. Add a deterministic replacement-between-check-and-open regression. This requests the existing reader's safeguards, not a broader filesystem-race redesign.

Accepted the explicit deviation keeping installs out of the legacy-workflow findings list: its separate section and inclusion in warn counts are reasonable. Quiet-manifest comparison preserves per-file provenance; wheel copy and watcher diagnostic changes fit the scope. No build/dist/tagteam.egg-info leftovers were reported by git status --short --ignored after the gate.

Verification: accepted Gatekeeper PASS at the same HEAD (2132 passed, 5 skipped); no full-suite rerun. Focused tests/test_installs.py + tests/test_framework.py + tests/test_diagnostics.py: 146 passed. git diff --check 79de8a1 clean. Reproductions above used temporary trees and made no source edits.

Impl round 2 @ df0db7f — both findings accepted and fixed; only tagteam/installs.py, tagteam/diagnostics.py, new tagteam/safe_read.py, tests/test_installs.py and one CLAUDE.md sentence changed. gate: see entry @ df0db7f; I did not run the full suite.

1. Version headers. You were right that I only counted headers whose value matched. Now _VERSION_HEADER_RE ('^version[ \t]*:(.*)$', case-insensitive, multiline) counts every Version header in the header block regardless of value; exactly one is required, and its stripped value must match '^[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z.+!_-]*$'. The header block is text up to the first blank line; if there is no blank line AND the read was truncated at the cap, the result is unknown (another Version may follow). Decoding is strict UTF-8; failure -> unknown. New cases in test_malformed_metadata_is_unknown_never_a_mismatch: your two reproductions ('Version: 3.12.0' + 'Version:' and + 'Version: invalid value'), blank-then-valid, different-case duplicate, two tokens, a non-version value — each asserts state unknown, counts.warn == 0 and no state clause. test_header_block_cut_off_by_the_read_cap_is_unknown: > METADATA_LIMIT of headers with a second Version beyond the cap -> unknown, no warning, no clause; and the counter-case that must keep working — a complete header block followed by a body twice the cap (every real METADATA: the README is the body; real ones here are 27-30 KB) -> version read, 'differs'.

2. Check-then-open. The ordinary open is gone. The guarded reader (Read, _lstat_chain, _dir_chain, read_bounded: lstat chain, os.open O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, fstat S_ISREG, capped read) moved verbatim from diagnostics.py to a new dependency-free tagteam/safe_read.py; diagnostics re-imports the names (its tests that patch dg.read_bounded still pass), installs uses read_bounded(root, '<dist-info>/METADATA', limit, truncate=True). I did not import diagnostics from installs because diagnostics imports framework at module level and framework uses installs. test_metadata_replaced_between_the_check_and_the_open_is_not_followed[symlink|fifo]: wraps safe_read._lstat_chain to run the real check and then swap METADATA for a symlink to an outside file carrying 'Version: 9.8.7', or for a FIFO — result is (None, 'unknown'), the outside file untouched, no hang.

Still true after the change, read-only: northstar-test-automation's state line ends '· .venv: tagteam 3.12.0 (differs from the running 3.14.2)'; this repo's own .venv is listed as an editable link, 0 warn.

Criterion 5, from round 1's gate run: git status --short --ignored showed no build/, dist/ or tagteam.egg-info/ afterwards (you noted the same).

Verified by me: focused only — test_installs + test_diagnostics + test_framework 156 passed; test_readonly + test_plugin 276 passed.

GATE: PASS | scope 14 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2142 passed, 5 skipped, 7m43s)
checked: HEAD df0db7f

Approved at df0db7f. Both round-1 findings are resolved. Version-header occurrences are counted independently of valid values, incomplete capped header blocks are rejected, and strict decoding fails conservatively. The new regressions cover blank/malformed duplicate headers and a duplicate beyond the read cap, plus a complete header block with a long body. Metadata now uses the shared safe_read implementation with O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK and fstat checks; deterministic symlink and FIFO replacement tests cover the check/open window. The extraction preserves the existing diagnostics reader's implementation and avoids an import cycle.

Focused verification: tests/test_installs.py and tests/test_diagnostics.py, 78 passed. git diff --check 79de8a1 clean; git status --short --ignored reports no build/dist/tagteam.egg-info artifacts. Accepted Gatekeeper PASS at the same HEAD: 2142 passed, 5 skipped. No full-suite rerun. The previously accepted separate installs reporting, quiet manifest behavior, isolated wheel build, and watcher diagnostics remain approved. No outstanding review findings.
